newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police urge restraint at HK-Japan soccer match.
newsitem.headline: HK police urge restraint at HK-Japan soccer match.

text.p: Hong Kong police cautioned fans on Monday to exercise restraint at a soccer match between a local side and a Japanese team in the wake of anti-Japanese protests over a group of disputed East China Sea islands.
A wave of anti-Japanese sentiment has swept Hong Kong, Macau and Chinese communities elsewhere over the islands claimed by Japan as the Senkakus and by China and Taiwan as the Diaoyus.

The movement has spiralled since Japanese extremists erected a lighthouse and planted flags on the islands in July. A Hong Kong man drowned when he leapt into the sea from a protest vessel last month.

Hong Kong demonstrators have staged a sit-in at the Japanese consulate and urged a boycott of Japanese goods. Some have stopped unsuspecting Japanese tourists along major shopping belts to hand them anti-Japanese leaflets.
The match between Hong Kong's South China team and Japan's Grampus Eight on Tuesday night is expected to attract tens of thousands of spectators, police said.

"In order to maintain a proper order during the event, police have liaised with the management of the stadium to implement appropriate crowd management measures," a police spokesman said in a statement.
"Sufficient police manpower will be deployed to carry out traffic and crowd management duties."
All national flags, of any nationality, and banners of all sizes would be prohibited from the stadium, the statement said.
